Failed ASR runs and retries must record analysis_run diagnostics and publish only run policy artifacts, never transcript artifacts. ExecutionPacket.purpose: Benchmark the representative long Telegram voice through the live API/worker/CopperASR path and convert resource failures into explicit blockers.
ExecutionPacket.contract-excerpt: The benchmark harness consumes representative_long_voice and records backend/model, input duration, wall time, CPU/memory samples, concurrency settings, compose resource limits, warm/cold model state, result delivery latency, threshold status, and blocker linkage when thresholds fail. The current evidence proves provider=copperasr, model=Copperside/CoppersideASR, 960.006s input, 165.319s run wall time, 5.807x realtime speed, transcript document delivery, duplicate-result guard, inbox clearing, and CopperASR response processing telemetry. The local consumer profile is COPPER_ASR_LOCAL_CPUS=4.0 plus COPPER_ASR_ONNX_NUM_THREADS=2, COPPER_ASR_TORCH_NUM_THREADS=2, COPPER_ASR_TORCH_INTEROP_THREADS=1, COPPER_ASR_FFMPEG_THREADS=1. The CPU threshold now passes inside copper-asr: max_cpu_percent=413.73, avg_cpu_percent=297.925, while worker-transcription and api stay near idle. The local image installs the CopperASR cpu extra, so upstream ONNX VAD provider delegation remains on the CPU provider for this compose profile. media-b8s.2.10 closed through a consumer compose CPU quota without editing the external CopperASR source submodule and without changing the max CPU benchmark semantics.

Generic backend-unavailable Telegram copy must not claim inbox content has already been saved; that saved-inbox copy is reserved for post-acceptance presentation recovery.
